See how you translated the similar expression in 5:11.

35.note: Yahweh is using **you have thrown me behind your back** as a common expression of the culture to mean “you have completely rejected me.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and you have utterly refused to have anything to do with me]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the **obscenity** and **prostitutions** of Oholibah were heavy loads that she **will carry**. It means that she will suffer the punishment for the evil things that she has done. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you will suffer the punishment for your obscenity and your prostitutions]
See how you translated the similar expression in 5:7.

36.note: Ezekiel is using the word translated as **Then** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

Yahweh is using the question form to tell Ezekiel that he should judge **Oholah and Oholibah**. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [you must judge Oholah and Oholibah!]

If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **abominations**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Then declare to them the abominable things they have done]
See how you translated the similar expression in [2:1](ta:02).

37.note: Here, **blood** represents “murder,” and having blood **on their hands** represents being guilty of murder. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and they are guilty of killing people]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if worshiping **idols** were committing adultery. It means that the people of Israel and Judah were unfaithful to Yahweh by worshiping other gods, just as a wife who commits adultery is unfaithful to her husband. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and by worshiping their idols, they have been unfaithful to me]
The pronoun **them** refers to the idols, not to the sons. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [they made pass through to their idols for food]

Yahweh is using **they made pass through to them** as a common expression of the culture to mean “they burned them as sacrifices to them.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [they burned as sacrifices to them for food]

38.q: ע֥וֹד זֹ֖את עָ֣שׂוּ לִ֑⁠י טִמְּא֤וּ אֶת מִקְדָּשִׁ⁠י֙ בַּ⁠יּ֣וֹם הַ⁠ה֔וּא
38.note: Here, **this** refers to what Yahweh says next. If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about what the people did before the information that **they did** it **to me**. Alternate translation: [Still they made my sanctuary unclean on that day; this is what they did to me]

39.note: The phrase **to profane it** indicates the result of their coming **to my sanctuary**, not the reason why they came. Use a connector in your language that makes this clear. Alternate translation: [and so profaned it]
Here, **my house** represents “my temple.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in the midst of my temple]

40.note: The expression **a messenger was sent** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the action, the context indicates that the two sisters did it. Alternate translation: [to whom they sent a messenger]

40.q: לַ⁠אֲשֶׁ֥ר רָחַ֛צְתְּ כָּחַ֥לְתְּ עֵינַ֖יִ⁠ךְ וְ⁠עָ֥דִית עֶֽדִי
40.note: The implication is that the woman **washed**, **painted your eyes**, and put on **ornaments** in order to make herself attractive to the men who came to her. This pictures the way the people of Judah tried to please the foreign nations whose help they wanted. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [those for whom you washed, you painted your eyes, and you adorned yourself with ornaments to make yourself attractive to them]

Yahweh has been speaking about the two sisters in the third person as **they**, but here he begins to speak to one of them directly in the second person as **you**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make it clear that Yahweh is now speaking directly to her. Alternate translation: [those for whom you, Oholibah, washed yourself]

41.q: וְ⁠יָשַׁבְתְּ֙ עַל מִטָּ֣ה כְבוּדָּ֔ה וְ⁠שֻׁלְחָ֥ן עָר֖וּךְ לְ⁠פָנֶ֑י⁠הָ
41.note: The implication is that the woman prepared a banquet for her lovers, where guests would recline on a couch beside a table of food. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And you reclined on a splendid couch at a banquet for your lovers, with a table of food arranged in front of it]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **bed** that is characterized by **glory**. It means a splendid couch. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a magnificent bed]

The expression **was arranged** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the action, the context indicates that the woman did it. Alternate translation: [with a table you had arranged in front of it]

The implication is that **my incense and my oil** were things that belonged to Yahweh and that people were supposed to use only to worship him. Instead, the woman used them to entertain her lovers. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and you set on it my incense and my oil, which were meant only for my worship]

42.note: The expression **were brought** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the action, you could use a general expression such as “people.” Alternate translation: [someone brought drunkards from the wilderness]

The word translated as **drunkards** is spelled almost the same in the original language as the word for Sabeans, a people who lived in the desert. The implication is that these men were either (1) drunkards who had come from the wilderness or (2) Sabeans who had come from the desert. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [drunkards, or Sabeans, were brought from the wilderness]

42.q: וַֽ⁠יִּתְּנ֤וּ צְמִידִים֙ אֶל יְדֵי⁠הֶ֔ן וַ⁠עֲטֶ֥רֶת תִּפְאֶ֖רֶת עַל רָאשֵׁי⁠הֶֽן
42.note: The pronoun **they** refers to the men who came to the women, while the pronoun **their** refers to the two sisters. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and those men put bracelets on the hands of the two sisters and a crown of beauty on the heads of the sisters]

43.q: וָ⁠אֹמַ֕ר לַ⁠בָּלָ֖ה נִֽאוּפִ֑ים עת יזנה תַזְנוּתֶ֖⁠הָ וָ⁠הִֽיא
43.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [And I said of the one worn out with adulteries that now even she would be used for prostitution by him]

Yahweh is using **the one worn out with adulteries** as a common expression of the culture to mean “the woman who has committed adultery so often that she has become old and tired.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [of the woman who has grown old and tired from committing adultery so often]

The meaning of **Now, he will prostitute her prostitutions, and she** is difficult to understand, and the words **and she** leave out a verb. The implication is either (1) that men will continue to use her as a prostitute even though she is worn out or (2) that she will continue to act as a prostitute. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Now men will keep on using her as a prostitute, even though she is worn out]

44.note: The pronoun **he** refers to each of the men who came to the woman, not to one specific man. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And each man went in to her]

Yahweh is referring to sexual relations in a polite way by using the phrase **went in to her**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [And he had sex with her]

The point of this comparison is that just as men go to **a prostituting woman** in order to have sexual relations with her, so men went **to Oholah and to Oholibah** for the same purpose. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [as men go to a prostitute in order to have sexual relations with her]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **women** who are characterized by **obscenity**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the obscene women]

45.note: Here, **pouring blood** represents “murdering people.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and with the judgment of those who murder people]
See how you translated the similar expression in 23:37.

46.q: הַעֲלֵ֤ה עֲלֵי⁠הֶם֙ קָהָ֔ל וְ⁠נָתֹ֥ן אֶתְ⁠הֶ֖ן לְ⁠זַעֲוָ֥ה וְ⁠לָ⁠בַֽז
46.note: The words translated as **Raise up** and **give** are imperatives, but they communicate what Yahweh will cause to happen rather than a command to a specific person. If the imperatives do not communicate this for your readers, then use a form in your language that communicates what will happen. Alternate translation: [An assembly will be raised up against them, and they will be given to terror and to plunder]
See how you translated the similar expression in 2:4.

47.q: וְ⁠רָגְמ֨וּ עֲלֵי⁠הֶ֥ן אֶ֨בֶן֙ קָהָ֔ל & בָּ⁠אֵ֥שׁ יִשְׂרֹֽפוּ
47.note: It might seem that the expressions **stone them with stones** and **with fire they will burn** contain extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten them. Alternate translation: [And an assembly will stone them … they will burn down]

The word **Their** refers to Oholah and Oholibah, not to the people of the **assembly**. The same is true of **their houses**. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [They will kill the sons and the daughters of Oholah and Oholibah, and they will burn the houses of those two women with fire]

48.note: The expression **will be warned** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who will do the action, the context indicates that Yahweh will do it. Alternate translation: [and I will warn all the women]

The implication is that **all the women** represents other nations and cities, which will learn from what happened to Samaria and Jerusalem and will not do what they did. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and all the women, that is, the other nations and cities, will be warned by what happened to you]

49.note: The word **you** is plural here because Yahweh is addressing both Oholah and Oholibah, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **sins** that are characterized by the worship of **your idols**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and the sins that you committed by worshiping your idols]
